newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent a lb higher while feeder cattle futures were called steady to up 0.200 cent, livestock analysts said.

Expectations that packers will show increased demand for fed cattle by Wednesday should keep live cattle futures supported. Packers appear to be somewhat short of slaughter- ready numbers, analysts said.
February was underpinned Monday on rolling of December longs and placing of a premium to cover possible problems from winter weather and this may continue, they said.
However, a steady to weak tone to boxed beef prices may weigh on sentiment, sources added.

Feeders cattle futures are seen showing carryover demand from the firm tone to feedlot cattle, reversal in the latest CME feeder cattle index and easier indications on corn futures. Demand for replacement feeders should remain firm based on fed sales and easing fed costs, analysts said.
The latest index was up $0.73 to $64.44 per cwt.
The market also looks technically strong after chart resistance points were penetrated chart resistance points Monday, they added.
